AEC Cybersecurity LEA.D8 · 420-D04-AB Conformity Assessment · Cohort CYB-01 · Fall 2026

Lab 1 — Identify the applicable laws, regulations and frameworks (10 %)

Step-by-step animations of what you do, in order, from the template download to the Omnivox LÉA DropBox. Due Sunday, November 8, 2026, 23:59 Eastern (EST). Files: LastName_FirstName_420-D04-AB_Lab1.pdf + .xlsx.

Use subject to the Cyber.SoHo Legal Notice, Terms of Use and Acceptable Use Policy v2.0 VT. All animations are self-made models, current to the end of October 2026; each carries a footnote on what may look different in your version.

Rules that never change

Cyber.SoHo Legal Notice, Terms of Use and Acceptable Use Policy v2.0 VT: education only — course work is not an audit of any real organization (sections 3, 7.5) · case file only, never an employer's or a family business's documents; real findings stay confidential (7.5, Annex E) · cite, never copy licensed standards (ISO/IEC 27001, PCI DSS) — article numbers only (4.6, 7.5) · lectures, templates and scripts are Cyber.SoHo intellectual property for personal study (section 4); your submission stays your copyright (18.3) · your own work, no real personal information, the College's rules on collaboration and AI tools apply (18) · check links with VirusTotal / Safe Browsing before opening them (14, Annex C) · no recording, no sharing of solutions with other cohorts (17). Short-form notice (Annex B): isolated, authorized lab environment only — the fictional case file and your own two VMs; unauthorized use of a computer system is a criminal offence (Criminal Code s. 342.1).

Lab base — download the files you need

The template workbook and the reference files from the Day 3 real-life examples. Blue rows in the workbook are worked examples.

Also needed: the one-page Érable Cycles case file (Day 1) and the Day 2 / Day 3 lecture pages. Alternatives to Microsoft 365: LibreOffice (free), Google Sheets / Docs (fictional data only); crosswalks: CIS Controls Navigator, NIST CPRT.

Step 1 — Set up (5 min)

Download Lab1_Template_420-D04-AB.xlsx and the reference files, rename the workbook with your name, create Lab1/evidence/. Every screenshot gets a unique name (L1-E01_…) and a line in the Evidence index tab; mask any real personal information.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): File Explorer (Windows 11 26H2) and Files (Ubuntu 24.04) look different from this model; the rename step is identical (F2 / right-click → Rename).

Step 2 — Part A: Applicability Register (Day 2; finish first)

One row per text: PIPEDA, Law 25, GDPR, PCI DSS v4.0.1, CASL (+ optional other). Applies? (Yes / Partly / No) with one sentence tied to a company fact; regulator; three obligations; two consequences; documentation required. The PCI DSS row is the worked example.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): Excel 365 (Microsoft 365, version 2510), LibreOffice Calc 25.8 and Google Sheets render the template the same way; formulas use only IF/AND/OR, available everywhere.

Step 3 — Part B.1: two frameworks in three sentences (10 min)

Default CIS Controls v8.1 IG1 + NIST CSF 2.0 Profile (alternative: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A). Sentence 1: size and expertise → IG1. Sentence 2: reporting and year-over-year progress → Profile. Sentence 3: PCI DSS applies anyway by contract, with a reduced scope.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): Optional: run python3 L1_csf_profile_gap.py with your own scores and quote the total gap.

Step 4 — Part B.2: mini traceability matrix (40 min)

Eight requirements from the register → the three given policies (Privacy Policy, Email Marketing Procedure, Payment Card Handling Policy) → control → evidence named now → test (Lab 3 method) → crosswalk references. The Status formula classifies each row; a draft policy is never an approved clause. At least two gaps are expected — explain each in one sentence.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): The live model of this matrix is L5_traceability_matrix.html (Lesson 5); the rule is the same four tests in the same order.

Step 5 — Part B.3: retention schedule (30 min)

Five record types, seven columns. Cite the legal minimum and maximum per row (Legal references sheet), write the period you recommend (not today's practice), the trigger, the disposal method, the owner (business role) and the legal-hold exception. All flags must read OK.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): PCI DSS 10.5.1 formally applies to systems in or connected to the cardholder-data environment; the course uses 12 months / 3 months online as the reference for all server and firewall logs.

Step 5 (optional) — check your periods with the Lesson 4 script

Edit L4_retention_schedule.csv (column applied_months = your recommended period, 9999 = indefinitely), then run python3 L4_retention_schedule.py. Every row must print OK; the summary line must read 0 and 0.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): Python 3.12 (Ubuntu 24.04) and 3.13 print identical output; on Windows use python instead of python3.

Step 6 — Assemble and export the Lab 1 document (20 min)

Title block (course, cohort, name, date, “course work — not an audit”) · 1 Register · 2 Frameworks · 3 Matrix + one sentence per gap · 4 Retention schedule · 5 Evidence index · 6 CPM Chapter 1 procedure (7-line skeleton). Export to PDF; keep the workbook as the second file. Maximum 4 pages.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): Menu names: LibreOffice Writer 25.8 → File ▸ Export As ▸ Export as PDF; Word (Microsoft 365) → File ▸ Save as ▸ PDF; Google Docs → File ▸ Download ▸ PDF. Older LibreOffice 24.x uses the same path.

Step 7 — Submit on Omnivox LÉA (5 min)

Omnivox → LÉA → 420-D04-AB → Assignments → Lab 1 → DropBox → add the PDF and the XLSX → Submit → screenshot the confirmation (L1-E30_submission.png). Deadline Sunday, November 8, 2026, 23:59 EST; −10 % per calendar day; a new submission before the deadline replaces the previous one.

Version footnote (end of October 2026): Omnivox LÉA screens differ by college and release (the model above is simplified; menu labels such as “Assignments” / “Travaux” and the DropBox button position vary). If the DropBox is closed, write to the professor before the deadline.

Self-check before you submit

  • ☐ 5 texts in the register, every reason tied to a company fact, nothing copied
  • ☐ 3 sentences: IG1 · CSF Profile · PCI DSS by contract
  • ☐ 8 matrix rows, status visible, ≥ 2 gaps explained, draft policy treated as a policy gap
  • ☐ 5 retention rows with minimum and maximum bases, all flags OK, owners are business roles
  • ☐ Evidence index filled, screenshots masked, CPM Chapter 1 in the 7-line skeleton
  • ☐ PDF ≤ 4 pages, correct file names, PDF + XLSX in the DropBox before Sunday 23:59 EST

Rubric (10): register 4 · frameworks 1 · matrix 2.5 · retention schedule 1.5 · clarity and CPM-ready format 1. Late: −10 % per calendar day.
